key_takeaways: Plan wedding lighting in three layers, in this order: ambient light for the whole space, accent light on tables, florals and architecture, then task light for paths, the bar and the speeches.
Look up the sunset time for your date at the destination, shoot portraits in golden hour, and have the ambient layer fully on before dusk so guests never sit in half light.

Each venue type asks for something different: festoons and uplit stone on a villa terrace, enclosed flame on a beach, festoons and uplit trees in a vineyard, dimmed chandeliers and pin spots in a ballroom.

Get the venue's open flame rule in writing, and in New South Wales, Victoria and Queensland check the state fire service's rules for fire ban days; overseas, check with your venue or planner and the local fire authority.
Ask for a lighting plan drawn for your venue and the hour you marry, with power, generator, wind and wet weather plans, rather than a standard package.

faq.q: What lighting is best for a wedding reception?
faq.a: Layered warm white light. Start with ambient light for the whole space (festoons, dimmed chandeliers or uplighting), add accent light on tables, florals and the cake, then task light for paths, the bar and the speeches. Keep every source warm white.

faq.q: How much lighting do you need for an outdoor wedding?
faq.a: Enough ambient light to see faces clearly after sunset, plus light on every path, step and the bar. The right amount depends on the space and what the venue already has, so ask your lighting supplier for a plan drawn for the site.

faq.q: Can you have real candles at a wedding venue?
faq.a: Only if the venue allows naked flame, so get its rule in writing; in New South Wales, the NSW Rural Fire Service says you cannot light a fire in the open on a Total Fire Ban day, so ask whether that covers table candles. In Victoria and Queensland, check the CFA or Queensland Fire Department rules; in other states and overseas, check with your venue or planner and the local fire authority.

faq.q: When should wedding lighting be turned on?
faq.a: Before dusk. Check the sunset time for your date at the destination and have the ambient layer fully on before the sun goes down.

faq.q: What is pin spotting at a wedding?
faq.a: Pin spotting is a narrow beam of light aimed at one object, such as a centrepiece or the cake, so it glows against the softer light of the room.
